The '''Sanyassa system''' was located in the [[Outer Moddell systems]] of the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell subsector]], one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]] within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]]. It lay on the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Bakura Trace/Legends|Bakura Trace]], which connected it to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor]] and [[Ast Kikorie system/Legends|Ast Kikorie systems]].<ref name="TEA" />

The [[Star system/Legends|system]] contained the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sanyassa IV]],<ref name="Gamer9" /> a lawless world that was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassan]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Sanyassa IV occupied the fourth [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position of the system, took 389 [[Local day/Legends|local days]] to complete one orbit, and was home to one billion of its natives.<ref name="TEA" /> By [[3963 BBY]], at least one Sanyassan, [[Bar'injar]], had made his way beyond Sanyassa IV<ref name="KOTOR 45">[[Knights of the Old Republic 45|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 45]]</ref> and into the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="TEA Volgax">[[Knights of the Old Republic 45|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 45]] depicts [[Bar'injar]] being present on [[Volgax]], and ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the corresponding [[Volgax system/Legends|Volgax system]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Sanyassa IV was first mentioned in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was authored by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Jason Fry]] and published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Gamer9" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], named the system and placed it in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
